HOW IT WORKS
  1. Connect a walletMetaMask, Phantom or any EVM wallet. Signing in is a message, never a transaction; you can watch every race without connecting at all.
  2. Join the racePick a marble, pick a name, press join. One marble per wallet, one race at a time: nobody is entered into a race they did not join.
  3. Watch it runThe camera chases the leaders down a track of ramps, spinners, jumps and boost pads. Every browser sees the same race at the same moment.
  4. Win the potFirst over the line takes the whole prize pool, paid to the winning address. The result and the address stay in the log.
  5. Vote the next trackTwo modes go up on the results screen. One vote per wallet; the winner is the next race's track, and the lobby shows it with a picture.
PROVABLY FAIR

The seed is fixed before anyone joins

The server publishes sha256(secret) when a race opens. When the queue closes, the seed is sha256(secret + the field) and the secret is revealed. Anyone can replay the race from the seed and check the winner.

          PROVABLY FAIR

          Nobody picks the winner. Not even us.

          Every race is decided by a seed that nobody can choose, and every race can be replayed by anyone, on any computer, to check that the marble that was paid is the marble that won.

          HOW THE SEED IS MADE
          1. A secret, before anyone joinsWhen a race opens the server draws a random secret and publishes only its hash, sha256(secret). The hash is on the lobby the whole time. The secret cannot change afterwards without the hash changing.
          2. The field closes, the seed is fixedWhen the queue closes, the seed is sha256(secret + "|" + the list of players). It depends on a secret fixed before anyone joined and on a field nobody can edit afterwards, so the server cannot look at who joined and pick a seed where its own wallet wins.
          3. The secret is revealedThe moment the race starts the secret is published with the seed. Anyone can hash it and compare it with the promise made at the start.
          4. The race is replayed everywhereThe same engine runs on the server and in every browser, using only arithmetic that every computer does identically. Given the seed and the field, the course, the start slots and every bounce come out the same, so the winner does too.

          The game mode is chosen by vote before the seed exists, so it changes nothing about this. Cheers are confetti: they are deliberately not part of the physics.

          VERIFY A RACE

          Pick a finished race. Your browser fetches its record, checks the hash, recomputes the seed and replays the race from it.

          Pick a race and press Verify.

          LAUNCHPAD

          Launch your own marble token.

          Launch a real token on Robinhood Chain through Pons, the chain's launchpad, from your own wallet: a name, a ticker, a picture, and one transaction. It trades from the first block and shows up on Pons, the explorer and the terminals that watch the Pons factory.

          LAUNCHES THROUGH PONS · ROBINHOOD CHAINYour wallet calls the Pons V2 factory. Fixed supply of 1,000,000,000, straight into a Pons bonding curve, which is the token's liquidity from the first block; when the curve fills, Pons graduates it into a locked Uniswap V4 pool on its own. Fee: quoted by Pons when you launch + gas.

          You pay the Pons launch fee and gas from your own wallet, on Robinhood Chain; the wallet switches network if it has to. An opening buy is a second transaction right after: your ETH goes into the token's curve as its first liquidity and the tokens come to your wallet, free of the launch-window snipe tax Pons charges everyone else. The token appears on Pons, on the Robinhood Chain explorer and on the terminals that watch the Pons factory. 70% of its trading fees go to your wallet by Pons' own rules. Nothing here ever sees your keys.

            HOW A LAUNCH WORKS
            1. Describe the tokenName, ticker, a description, a picture and your links. That is what goes on-chain, in the launch call itself.
            2. Launch on PonsYour wallet switches to Robinhood Chain if it has to, quotes the Pons launch fee, and sends one transaction to the Pons V2 factory. The token and its bonding curve are deployed in that transaction.
            3. Check it anywhereThe page shows the contract address, the transaction and links to the explorer and Pons. Terminals that index Pons launches list it on their own.
            4. Earn from tradesEvery trade pays a fee and 70% of it goes to the wallet that launched, by Pons' own rules. Buyback & lock, if on, turns part of it into a locked position.
            WHAT THE PAD NEVER DOES

            Your keys stay in your wallet

            The launchpad never asks for a private key or a seed phrase, never signs on your behalf, and never shows a transaction that did not happen. Launching is one transaction you approve in your own wallet, paid from your own balance, and every result on this page is read back from the receipt.
